messages.author: 3cb8e5cfad3e6a9f
messages.subject: Interaction plot & bar plot
parts: Hi, does anyone know how to draw a bar plot which looks like an interaction plot and have two categorical independent variables and one interval dependent variable? Thanks!

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] Interaction plot & bar plot
parts: > Hi, does anyone know how to draw a bar plot which looks like an interaction plot and have two categorical independent variables and one interval dependent variable? Thanks!

Like this?

rm(list=ls(all=TRUE)); set.seed(1)
dv <- rnorm(200)
iv1 <- factor(sample(letters[1:2], 200, replace=TRUE))
iv2 <- factor(sample(letters[11:12], 200, replace=TRUE))
(qwe <- tapply(dv, list(iv1, iv2), mean))
barplot(qwe, beside=TRUE)

Best,
STG

parts: set.seed is for setting a seed ;) for the pseudo-random generator in your computer. That way you always get the same "random" numbers. rnorm produces random numbers based on the normal distribution, tapply applies a function to a data set but by groups according to a given factor. I'd suggest using "?rnorm", "?set.seed", and "?tapply".
